messages:
liz: Heads-up — ACME asked for a Gold-tier enterprise commit design. They expect ~1500 requests/min peak for a mix of chat (LLM gen) and embeddings. Need: reserved GPU sizing, autoscale policy, preheat plan, and an answer for the security questionnaire window. Can we sync POC ops + pricing?
raja: Quick math: 1500 req/min = 25 req/sec. If average chat request = 120 tokens out / 40 in ~ 160 tokens total, and embeddings are cheap but frequent. What's traffic split chat:embedding?
gwen: ACME said 70% chat, 30% embeddings. Chat concurrency matters more. Typical tail concurrency multiplier = peak RPS * avg latency. If we target p95 latency <= 250ms for chat, per-request GPU time ≈ 0.25s (very rough). So 25 req/s * 0.25s = 6.25 GPU-seconds/s -> ~6.25 GPUs worth baseline without batching. With batching (batch=8 avg) we can cut GPU count by ~3x.
samir: For reserved pool plan I'd propose: 3x A100-equivalent reserved nodes with burst credits and autoscale up to 6 for sustained surges. Rationale: baseline 2 reserved + 1 buffer. Autoscale policy short cooldowns.
liz: Can you put that as quick config snippet I can send to customer? Also need cost ballpark for sales (monthly).
raja: Sure — config sketch (pseudo):
```
reserved_pool: size: 3
autoscale: min: 3
          max: 6
          scale_up_policy: rps > 30 for 30s -> +1
          scale_down_policy: rps < 20 for 2m -> -1
preheat: enabled: true
        prewarm_on_deploy: 1
        preheat_window_secs: 300
fallbacks: model_variant: medium-quantized -> route if latency > 400ms
```
gwen: Preheat windows: recommend warm KV caches for typical conversation prefixes. For chat-heavy traffic, preheat cache for top ~10 prompts (customer will share examples). That shaves initial 200-400ms cold penalty. :thumbsup:
samir: Cost note: rough reserved cost = (3 reserved A100-equivalent) ~ $Xk/month; burst capacity billed at usage. I'll compute more precise numbers after we pick exact instance type and expected token/sec.
liz: Also security questionnaire: they asked about key management and private telemetry. We should offer Private deployment/VPC option as an enterprise add-on and mention KMS integration + audit logs. Who owns the questionnaire answers?
gwen: I can own the security responses. I'll draft answers for KMS, network isolation, data-at-rest, access logs. Send me the questionnaire and any customer SLA asks.
raja: POC ops: we need a runbook for failure modes — autoscale lag, batch buildup, OOMs. Quick checklist:
- establish traffic replay from customer test harness (1 hour window)
- run synthetic peaked burst (2x expected)
- validate fallback model routing works
- measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token/sec
- verify cache preheat reduces cold p95
- snapshot logs + tracing for handover
samir: ops-bot: scheduled a POC kickoff meeting for Fri 10am PT and created a ticket: POC-4832. Please confirm attendees.
liz: I'll invite ACME, product, security (gwen), infra (raja), and SRE (samir). Also need a simple pricing slide: reserved upfront discount + overage rate. I'll draft it if you share the cost calc.
gwen: I'll start the security answers now. Raja/samir — please share expected instance choices and perf numbers.
raja: Sending perf samples and quantized vs float benchmarks in thread: link: https://internal.redwood/perf/acme-benchmarks -> use medium-quant for cost-sensitive fallback.
liz: Awesome. Action items: gwen -> security Qs, raja -> perf + exact instance cost, samir -> ops runbook + POC ticket details. I'll bundle config + pricing slide and send to ACME before Friday. :rocket:
